headline: LLM Training Achieved on Inference-Only NPUs, Bypassing GPUs Entirely
summary: VIDRAFT's VKORE-46M-NPU model was pre-trained from scratch using only inference-dedicated hardware, challenging conventional ML training paradigms.
details: VIDRAFT has achieved a significant breakthrough by successfully pre-training a small language model (SLM) entirely on inference-only NPUs, a feat previously thought impossible. The model, named VKORE-46M-NPU, bypasses GPUs at every stage of training and is now publicly available on Hugging Face.

This achievement challenges the conventional wisdom that inference-only NPUs are unsuitable for training workloads. These chips are typically designed for efficient forward passes, lacking the hardware features for gradient computation and weight updates required by backpropagation.

The VKORE-46M-NPU, a 46-million-parameter model, was trained on a public dataset and can generate short English-language stories. VIDRAFT is developing VKORE, an NPU-native acceleration software layer, aiming to provide NPU functionality similar to CUDA for NVIDIA GPUs.

A key quantitative result highlighted by VIDRAFT is a 0.99 loss correlation between the NPU-trained and GPU-trained runs. This indicates that the NPU-based training process converges along a statistically near-identical path, validating the numerical consistency of the gradient computation.

It is crucial to note that this correlation does not imply parity in training speed. VIDRAFT explicitly clarifies that inference-only NPUs are generally slower for training workloads, and this result focuses on correctness validation rather than speed benchmarking.

VIDRAFT has also verified that general-purpose public models can run inference and quantized-model execution on the same NPU hardware, suggesting the VKORE layer supports both training and deployment lifecycles.

While the trained model weights and analysis materials are public on Hugging Face, the core training code is withheld for IP protection. A technical paper detailing the implementation is planned for future release, and there is no mention of a public API endpoint for this specific model at this time.
